fichas.title: Water spray extinguisher systems
fichas.summary: Permanently installed dry pipework with open nozzles releases water immediately when activated. Spray pattern and coverage are designed for the room, building, contents, storage, and wind conditions. Systems are grouped to protect areas and can supply nearby group areas simultaneously.
uses: Protect buildings, industrial facilities, flammable-liquid systems, and other listed areas from fire

FIRE PROTECTION
Other Extinguisher Systems

Water spray extinguisher systems
Water spray extinguisher systems are water distribution systems
with permanently installed pipework, on which open nozzles
are mounted at regular intervals. When the system is on standby,
the pipework is not filled with water. When the system is activated,
this immediately releases the peak flow from the water supply
into the pipework.
The water spray pattern is based on the shape and dimensions of
the room to be protected, the type of building, type and quantity
of goods to be protected, height and type of storage, and wind
influence, and must spray at a rate of 5-60 l/m 2/min.

Powder extinguisher systems
Fire extinguisher powders are homogenous mixtures of
chemicals which are suitable for fighting fires. The main
ingredients are sodium/potassium bicarbonate, potassium
sulphate, potassium/sodium chloride and ammonium phosphate/
sulphate.
Because the extinguisher powder can be used under normal
conditions at temperatures from -20 to +60°C, it is employed in
buildings, enclosed rooms and also in open-air areas of industrial
plants.

The essential parameters of a foam extinguisher system are:
water quantity, foaming agent consumption, foam ratio (ratio of
foam to water-foaming agent mixture) and minimum operating
time. When systems with medium and heavy foam are used, the
foam must be able to cover the entire area to be foamed, taking
into account the flowing and throwing range, any obstacles, and
the distance and type of object to be protected. When systems
with light foam are used, the foam must be able to effectively fill
the room or building.
If a number of separate objects are to be protected by the same
foam extinguisher system, the water supply requirement is
designed for the largest single object. The water supply must be
designed for operation for at least 120 min for heavy foam and
60 min for medium foam. (VdS Guidelines 2108)

fichas.title: Oxygen-reducing extinguisher systems (CO₂ systems)
fichas.summary: Oxygen-reducing systems suppress combustion by lowering the oxygen content. The page describes CO₂ as a gaseous fire-fighting agent delivered rapidly through installed pipework and open nozzles, with detection, control, alarm, and activation equipment. Safety is critical because concentrations above 5% are described as lethal and strongly corrosive.
uses: Suppress developing fires and maintain CO₂ concentration to prevent reignition
Protect rooms and areas from fires involving combustible liquids, gases, electrical and electronic equipment, and some solid materials
furniture_equipment: Fire detection, control, alarm, and activation equipment

dimensions.label: Maximum floor area supplied per nozzle
dimensions.context: For systems intended to protect rooms, one nozzle may supply at most this floor area.

dimensions.label: Room height threshold
dimensions.context: For rooms higher than this, nozzles are installed at the ceiling and also at approximately one-third of room height.

The essential parameters of a foam extinguisher system are:
water quantity, foaming agent consumption, foam ratio (ratio of
foam to water-foaming agent mixture) and minimum operating
time. When systems with medium and heavy foam are used, the
foam must be able to cover the entire area to be foamed, taking
into account the flowing and throwing range, any obstacles, and
the distance and type of object to be protected. When systems
with light foam are used, the foam must be able to effectively fill
the room or building.
If a number of separate objects are to be protected by the same
foam extinguisher system, the water supply requirement is
designed for the largest single object. The water supply must be
designed for operation for at least 120 min for heavy foam and
60 min for medium foam. (VdS Guidelines 2108)
